subject: Multi-region Dedicated capacity: commit structuring, DR replication credits & routing
messages:
From: Sofia Rojas <sofia.rojas@atlashealth.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Multi-region Dedicated capacity for Atlas Health — sizing & DR

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this — quick summary of our needs from the product/infra side at Atlas Health: we run a clinician-facing notes ingestion and summarization pipeline with strict latency targets (95th < 350ms) and regional residency requirements for PHI. We need dedicated capacity in two regions: us-east (primary) and eu-west (secondary) with the ability to failover in < 60s.

Key asks:
- Separate reserved GPU pools per region (no shared cross-region burst).
- Throughput guarantee: sustained 120 tok/s equivalent (model: open-llm LLaMA-3-13B) per region with 95% availability SLA.
- Replication/DR: warm standby in EU with automated routing on failover.
- Pricing/commits: we prefer a 12-month reserved commit but need to understand breakage credits, cross-region replication costs, and any egress/replication credits you can provide.
- Contractual: SOC 2 Type II evidence, KMS support, and audit logs.

Rough expected baseline: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs in us-east, 8 in eu-west.

Can you send a pricing outline and options (active-active, warm-standby), and any concessions on replication charges if we commit?

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Rojas
Head of Platform Engineering, Atlas Health
sofia.rojas@atlashealth.ai

Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated capacity for Atlas Health — sizing & DR

Hi Sofia — thanks, and great context.

High level options (summary attached as PDF):

Option A — Separate pools + warm standby (recommended initial approach)
- Provision: US-east: 16 GPU reserved commit; EU-west: 8 GPU reserved commit (separate pools).
- Replication: asynchronous KV/prefix replication for model warm-priming + periodic KV syncs; automatic route failover to EU pool on health failure.
- SLA: per-pool throughput SLO (95% availability) with credits tied to observed token throughput.
- Pricing: standard reserved rate per-GPU; replication egress billed at cost tier but we can offer a replication credit (see below).

Option B — Active-active / geo-load-balanced
- Provision: mirrored capacity in both regions sized for steady-state traffic (higher cost).
- Consistent low-latency routing with cross-region routing for some sessions.
- Pricing: premium + cross-region egress.

Concessions we can offer if Atlas signs a 12-month reserved commit today:
- 20% committed usage discount on per-GPU reserved rate (applies to both regions).
- Replication credit: waive first 6 months of cross-region replication egress up to 10TB/month.
- Onboarding credit: one month of complimentary burst capacity for model warm-ups.

If Atlas is open to a 24-month commit, we can increase the discount to 30% and extend replication credit to 12 months.

Next steps:
1) See attached pricing summary (Atlas_Redwood_Dedicated_PRICING_v1.pdf) with a line-item math for 16/8 commit sizing.
2) Quick call to align SLAs and operational runbook — can you do Thu 10/15 or Fri 10/16?
3) If the terms look OK, we’ll draft a Master Services Order and a DocuSign link for signature.

Notes: we can also scope a small pilot (75% reserved / 25% burst) if you want to de-risk.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: Multi-region Dedicated capacity for Atlas Health — internal ask on pricing tweaks

Internal — forwarding the thread and my suggested adjustments before I reply back to Sofia with concrete numbers. Please keep this internal; we are still negotiating.

Key points / rationale:
- Atlas baseline request ~= 16 + 8 GPUs. If we price at standard reserved rate $X/GPU/mo, the list is aggressive for 12-month term.
- Proposal A: 12-month commit (16 US | 8 EU) -> 20% discount. Offer replication credit: waive cross-region egress up to 10TB/mo for first 6 months.
- Proposal B: 24-month commit -> 30% discount + replication credit extended to 12 months; include a 2-month termination notice in SOW to protect capacity.
- Technical note from Karthik: warm-standby replication uses prefix/KV snapshotting — recommended to limit full-model sync frequency (nightly) and use warm checkpoints for fast failover. This keeps egress low.

Ask: Marissa — can you flag whether Legal is OK with the 2-month termination clause and the replication-credit wording? Karthik — confirm the estimated egress number for a warm-standby for their traffic profile (ballpark TB/month).

I attached a proposed pricing worksheet to show the math (proposed_pricing_sheet.xlsx).

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated capacity for Atlas Health — sizing & DR

Irene — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. We’re broadly comfortable with Option A + the 12-month commit at the 20% discount. A couple of clarifications before we move to signature:

1) Can you confirm the exact per-GPU monthly rate after discount in the attached worksheet? I want to ensure the total monthly commit number aligns with our procurement threshold.
2) We appreciate the 6-month replication credit. Can we instead have that credit apply to cross-region egress and replicated KV bandwidth equally (i.e., combined cap 10TB/mo)?
3) On the SLA/credits: we’ll need the SLA language in the SOW that maps availability to token throughput (so we can show our compliance team).

If those items are ok, we’ll route this internally and ask Procurement to sign DocuSign next week.

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Rojas
